members.title: Docstrings say "fourteen" value columns; the mapping has sixteen
members.description:
`CandleRow` says it holds "the fourteen value columns." `models/kalshi_timeseries.py:5` says "the fourteen flat stored columns," and `test_kalshi_models.py:186` says "The fourteen values." `CANDLE_COLUMNS` (`candle_repository.py:50-62`) has sixteen entries: fourteen nested OHLC, previous, and mean columns, plus `volume_fp` and `open_interest_fp`. `constants.py:1306` says sixteen, and the candle test asserts `len(values) == len(CANDLE_COLUMNS)`. The code is right and the prose is wrong.

Fix: correct the three docstrings to "sixteen" (or "fourteen nested, two flat").

members.title: Functions and files grew well past the length guideline
members.description: `_execute_summary` runs about 210 lines (from line 187 to the end of the 398-line file). `_dispatch_via_session` runs about 105 lines (`dispatch.py:515-620`), and `dispatch.py` is now 931 lines. The guide asks for roughly 50-line functions and 300-line files. Part of the length predates this diff, but the diff adds usage branching to both functions. Fix: extract the SDK-versus-one-shot capture block into helpers in `usage_capture.py`, and extract the session record building out of `_dispatch_via_session`.

members.title: `dispatch.py` is now 931 lines
members.description: CLAUDE.md asks for source files of about 300 lines where practical. The file was already well over that, and this diff adds session capture, one-shot capture, the provider-failure mapping, and the `_one_shot` wrapper to it. Consider moving the usage plumbing or the session path into their own modules.

members.title: Two functions are well past the length guideline, and this diff grew both
members.description:
`_execute_summary` runs from line 187 to line 395, about 210 lines. This diff adds usage capture to both its SDK and one-shot branches. `_dispatch_via_session` (`dispatch.py:515-620`) is about 105 lines and also grew here. CLAUDE.md asks for functions of about 50 lines.

Fix: extract each branch's capture-and-stamp step into a helper that returns the text and its metadata.

members.title: `_locked` builds a coroutine before the lock is taken, then closes it on failure
members.description: `_locked` receives an already-created coroutine and must call `run_coroutine.close()` if the lock is refused. `ExitStack` and `_take_run_lock(stack, ...)` wrap what is really one optional context manager. This contradicts the project rule to resist complexity. Pass a zero-argument factory, or use `with project_run_lock(os.getcwd()) if pipeline_mutates(definition) else nullcontext():`. Then no coroutine can be left unawaited and the `ExitStack` goes away. Five call sites would simplify.

members.title: Item resume writes the batch run's state as if it were a new step result
members.description:
`_run_pipeline` skips `init_run` when a `run_id` is given (`run.py:238`), but it still calls `state_mgr.finalize(run_id, result)` (`run.py:279`). The step callback also appends a `slices` StepState (`state.py:319`). Two effects follow:

- The run's terminal status becomes the result of this one item.
- After a git halt the batch run has no `slices` entry, because `on_step_complete` runs only on normal return (`executor.py:576-577`). Item resume appends one, so `first_unfinished_step` (`state.py:459-471`) returns None. A later plain `sq run --resume <id>` then prints "All steps already completed" while items are still `not_run`.

Unless D8 intends this, item resume should not finalize the run or append a step to it. The item-resume tests miss it: `tests/pipeline/item_resume_support.py` `body_runner` calls `execute_pipeline` directly, never reaches `_run_pipeline`, and omits the `from_step` argument that production passes (`run_item.py:84`).

members.title: `ItemRerun.replace` raises a bare `StopIteration` when the index is missing
members.description: `next(i for i, r in enumerate(records) if r.index == record.index)` has no default. If the index is absent, `StopIteration` escapes. Inside the coroutine that becomes an opaque `RuntimeError`, and it fires from the `finally` handling in `_finish_each_report`, where it could mask the original fault. `_reconcile` has the same pattern. Raise an explicit error naming the index instead.

members.title: Unreachable code and a fragile `next()` inside coroutines
members.description: `raise AssertionError("unreachable")` after the `with ExitStack()` block is dead code. The block always returns or raises, so it only exists to quiet a type checker. Separately, `ItemRerun.replace` and `_outcome` use bare `next(...)` with no default. If the record is missing, a `StopIteration` raised inside a coroutine surfaces as an opaque `RuntimeError`. An explicit error would honor the fail-fast and "name the fact" convention the rest of the module follows.

members.title: `test_setup_backup.py` has grown to 1072 lines
members.description: This diff adds roughly 250 lines to a file that already exceeded the ~300-line guideline. Split it by subject: argument parsing, the cluster table, render, and lifecycle.

members.title: Exception-to-exit-code mapping depends on a caller-supplied tuple
members.description: `run_mapped` checks `isinstance(exc, storage)` before `exit_code_for`. This lets `TickDatabaseUnreachable` override the "preflight" mapping for the read verbs only. It works, and `tick_exit.py` already maps `TickCalendarError` and `psycopg.OperationalError` to storage. However, exit-code policy is now split between `tick_exit.py`, which the design says defines it once, and a per-verb parameter. `_read_storage()` also needs a function-local import just to build a one-element tuple. A cleaner option is a dedicated `TickReadUnreachable` exception, or a `read_only` flag passed to `exit_code_for`. As written, the "one place" invariant is weakened.

members.title: `run_mapped` storage override is order-dependent
members.description: `TickDatabaseUnreachable` subclasses `TickPreflightError`, so `exit_code_for` still returns exit 1 for it in the writers. The read verbs get exit 4 only because they pass a `storage` tuple to `run_mapped`. Exit-code mapping is now split between `tick_exit.exit_code_for` and a per-call override, which cuts against the "defined once, in `tick_exit.py`" statement in the module docstring. Handling the subclass in `exit_code_for` would keep one source of truth. The writers would need a decision on whether unreachable means exit 1 or 4 there too. The behaviour is tested and the override is documented, so this is a design smell and not a bug.

members.title: Cron comparison prevents recovery by rerunning the cutover
members.description: `production_changes()` strips new arguments only from `new`. After cron installation, a rerun captures the already-updated file as `old`, so identical cron files compare as different and step 4 fails. This blocks the documented recovery path for failures in later steps. Normalize both sides and add a post-installation rerun regression test.

members.title: Production comparison rejects every post-install rerun
members.description: Only the new cron lines have their added arguments stripped. After the first installation, `step_check` captures already-updated lines as `old`, so comparing an unchanged installed file against itself reports differences and stops step 4. This was reproduced with the helper. Normalize both sides and add an already-installed rerun test.

members.title: Re-running after cron installation always fails
members.description: Only the new cron lines have their added arguments stripped. On a rerun, `ctx.old_cron` already contains those arguments, so comparing an unchanged post-cutover file against itself reports differences and aborts step 4. This prevents the documented recovery procedure after any later failure. Normalize both sides and add a post-cutover rerun regression test.

members.title: The cutover's own repair/verify command is not covered by the sudoers rule
members.description: `_repair` runs `sudo /opt/manta-trading/.venv/bin/python scripts/repair_921_minute_sessions.py <mode>` (lines 96-100). No rule in `deploy/sudoers.d/manta-ops` matches that interpreter path. Sudo will therefore prompt for a password on `--check`, `--apply`, and each `--verify` poll. `_verify_when_fresh` polls for up to 75 minutes, and the credential timestamp lapses after 5 minutes by default. Unattended or non-interactive runs will fail or stall. Add the exact argv and verify with `sudo -l -U manta`.

members.title: The sudoers rule does not match what the scripts actually run
members.description: The header says the rule covers "exactly the commands those scripts issue". But `_repair` runs `sudo /opt/manta-trading/.venv/bin/python scripts/repair_921_minute_sessions.py <mode>`, and no rule covers that interpreter. Each repair and verify call falls back to a password prompt, and `sudo -n` fails. The installer path also disagrees: `install()` resolves it from `__file__` (scripts/cutover_common.py:134), while the rule hard-codes one checkout path, so running from any other checkout (including a worktree) prompts for a password. Add the interpreter, narrowly, for this script's three modes. Either pin the installer location or document that the checkout must match.

members.title: The sudoers rule does not cover the repair step, and its header claim is inaccurate
members.description:
The header says the rule covers "Exactly the commands those scripts issue." It does not. `_repair` (`scripts/cutover_921_minute_sessions.py:96-100`) runs `sudo /opt/manta-trading/.venv/bin/python scripts/repair_921_minute_sessions.py <mode>` on every `--check`, `--apply` and `--verify`. None of the aliases match that command, so the cutover prompts for a password at its first repair step, or fails without a TTY. In the other direction, `MT_UNITS` lists `systemctl is-active`, which `unit_active` never runs under sudo.

Fix: run the repair as the service user (`sudo -u manta-trading ...`), which is the same pattern as `MT_GIT`, and add that alias. Do not grant root to a repository script.

members.title: Sudoers rule omits a command the cutover issues, and exposes the env file
members.description:
`_repair` in `scripts/cutover_921_minute_sessions.py:96-100` runs `sudo /opt/manta-trading/.venv/bin/python scripts/repair_921_minute_sessions.py <mode>`. No alias covers it. It would prompt for a password, with stdout and stderr captured, in the middle of an unattended cutover. The header's "exactly the commands those scripts issue" is therefore false.

`MT_READ` grants `cat /etc/manta-trading.env` as root. That file holds all production credentials, including the maintenance DB URL. This works against the project's split-role principle, and the file should not be readable this way.

members.title: Fan-out usage is discarded before persistence
members.description: Passing the capture into branches records usage temporarily, but the fan-in reducers discard action metadata. The successful executor result retains only the reduced action; failed branches return an empty action list. A `CollectReducer` probe confirmed empty metadata despite populated branch usage. Preserve all branch usage independently of the selected output and test both successful and failed fan-outs.
